doc.title: Jon Hendricks interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 29, 2000 [interview 2 of 2]

title: The vocalese program at the University of Toledo
summary: Plans a vocalese studies program with Hank Jones, Ray Brown and Max Roach as rhythm section.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: Amazing. You’ve got some great news regarding your vocalese school?

Oh yeah. I’m waiting for my federal papers to come back, and then the University of Toledo has engaged me to start in the fall, next fall, and I want to have the vocalese studies program start there. And from there we will proliferate all over the world. Because I’ve already made arrangements to have a rhythm section of Hank Jones, Ray Brown and Max Roach have all agreed to be the rhythm section for 2001.
Gee you couldn’t get anybody good.

So jazz students from all over the world are coming to that school. Because I have students from all over the world asking me about studies. My singer, Kevin Burke, married a Japanese girl who now teaches with him. She came over her to study under me. And I told her I don’t give personal lessons. So there’s going to be students from all over the world coming to the University of Toledo when we start that program.

Let me throw a little scenario at you here. You’re in front of the college’s Board of Trustees trying to pitch your idea. And as well meaning as they might be, they don’t have a clue what vocalese really is.
So what do you tell them? © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -18-
